'''Acroá''' is an extinct [[Central Jê languages|Akuwẽ (Central Jê)]] language ([[Jê languages|Jê]], [[Macro-Jê languages|Macro-Jê]]) of [[Brazil]]. It was spoken by the Acroá people around the headwaters of the [[Parnaíba River|Parnaíba]] and of the [[Paranaíba River|Paranaíba]] in [[Bahia]], who were later settled in the missions of [[Dianópolis|São José do Duro (Formiga)]] and in [[Mossâmedes|São José de Mossâmedes]]. The language went extinct before it could be properly documented; it is only known through a short wordlist collected by [[Carl Friedrich Philipp von Martius]].<ref name="Nikulin-Macro-Je">{{cite thesis|last=Nikulin |first=Andrey |date=2020 |url=http://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/tese%3Anikulin-2020/Nikulin_2020_Proto-Macro-Je.pdf |title=Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo |type=Ph.D. dissertation |location=Brasília |publisher=Universidade de Brasília}}</ref>{{rp|14}} Due to an account of Martius' travels appearing in three large volumes from 1823 to 1831, the language probably went extinct sometime around then. Acroá is also known as '''Akroá''', '''Acroamirim''', '''Coroá''' and '''Koroá'''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Akroá|publisher=[[Linguist List|LINGUIST List]]|access-date=4 November 2024|archive-date=26 August 2012|url-status=dead|url=http://multitree.org/codes/acs.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120826012525/http://multitree.org/codes/acs.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Carvalho |first=Fernando Orphão de |last2=Damulakis |first2=Gean Nunes |date=2015-01-05 |title=The Structure of Akroá and Xakriabá and their relation to Xavante and Xerente: a contribution to the historical linguistics of the Jê languages |url=http://periodicos.sbu.unicamp.br/ojs/index.php/liames/article/view/8641494 |journal=LIAMES: Línguas Indígenas Americanas |language=pt |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=17–46 |doi=10.20396/liames.v15i1.8641494 |issn=2177-7160|doi-access=free }}</ref>
